description:
In the 2025-26 season, Zach Werenski — the dynamic defenseman from Grosse Pointe, Mich., who anchored the Columbus Blue Jackets’ blue line — delivered an incredible campaign that earned him his first Norris Trophy.
Featured in this highlight are three standout moments showcasing his tremendous skill set. First, Werenski’s shootout goal to clinch the win in Detroit, a pinpoint shot that silenced the Detroit crowd. Next, his first assist versus Ottawa, where he eluded multiple defenders and drew all the attention before sending the puck over to the front of the net for the tip-in goal. Finally, his second goal against Minnesota, where he anticipated the play in the neutral zone, jumped the pass to intercept it near center ice, then skated down the ice and fired a wrist shot post-and-in for the unassisted goal.
Werenski’s two-way dominance and offensive production throughout the season made him the first Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman to ever win the Norris Trophy, cementing his legacy as one of the League’s premier defensemen.
